source.usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2026' (pages 1-14) or 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2026' (pages 15-29); examYear 2026 is the examination year the specimen is published for. Listed on cisce.org under specimen-question-papers-isc-class-xii-2026. The similarly named 2025_08_860-MATHEMATICS-SQP-AK-1.pdf is a different document (ISC Class XI specimen 2026) and was not used. 'page' is the physical PDF page of the question. The paper prints 'Maximum Marks: 80', three hours, 22 questions: Section A (65 marks, compulsory, Q1-Q14) and either Section B (Q15-Q18) or Section C (Q19-Q22), 15 marks each; the pack contains both B and C, so the summed marks (one alternative per OR group) are 95. OR alternatives are labelled (i)/(ii) as printed and share choiceGroup = question number. Cognitive tags (Understanding, Recall, Application, Analysis, Evaluate) are printed in green beside each question and are reproduced as printed. Multi-part questions whose parts share one scenario (Q10, Q11, Q13, Q14, Q16(i), Q22) are kept as single entries with their parts in the text. pdftotext dropped several lines on some pages (e.g. the stems of Q1(iii), Q10(ii), Q22); the full text was taken from the pdfplumber text layer and checked against the rendered pages. Fractions, powers, matrices and integral limits collapse in the text layer and were rebuilt inline from the rendered pages (flagged per question). Regression (Q19(ii), Q19(iii), Q21) and break-even (Q19(v)) have no matching chapter slug and are left with chapter null.

questions.text: Find the point on the curve y = (x − 2)² at which the tangent is parallel to the chord joining the end points (2,0) and (4,4).
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF (letter-spaced 'a t w h i c h t h e' in the text layer joined as 'at which the')
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: y = (x − 2)²; dy/dx = 2(x − 2). Slope of the chord = (4−0)/(4−2) = 2. Let P(x₁, y₁) be the point on the curve. Since the tangent is parallel to the chord. Therefore, their slopes are equal. ∴ 2(x₁ − 2) = 2 ⟹ x₁ = 3 and y₁ = 1. So, the point P is (3,1).

questions.text: Solve: sin⁻¹(x) + sin⁻¹(1 − x) = cos⁻¹ x.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: sin⁻¹(x) + sin⁻¹(1 − x) = cos⁻¹ x ⇒ sin⁻¹(x) + sin⁻¹(1 − x) = π/2 − sin⁻¹ x ⇒ sin⁻¹(1 − x) = π/2 − 2 sin⁻¹ x ⇒ (1 − x) = sin(π/2 − 2 sin⁻¹ x) ⇒ (1 − x) = cos(2 sin⁻¹ x) ⇒ (1 − x) = cos(cos⁻¹(1 − 2x²)) ⇒ (1 − x) = 1 − 2x² ⇒ 2x² − x = 0 ∴ x = 0, 1/2

questions.text: If y = (A + Bx)e⁻²ˣ, prove that: d²y/dx² + 4 dy/dx + 4y = 0
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF (the text layer scrambles d²y/dx² as 'dx2 d2y')
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: Given, y = (A + Bx)e⁻²ˣ. Differentiating w.r.t ‘x’ ⟹ dy/dx = (A + Bx)(−2e⁻²ˣ) + e⁻²ˣB ⟹ dy/dx = (−2y) + e⁻²ˣB ⟹ dy/dx + 2y = e⁻²ˣB (i). Differentiating w.r.t ‘x’ ⟹ d²y/dx² + 2 dy/dx = −2e⁻²ˣB (ii). (i) and (ii) ⟹ d²y/dx² + 2 dy/dx = −2(dy/dx + 2y) ⟹ d²y/dx² + 4 dy/dx + 4y = 0, Hence Proved.

questions.text:
Solve the following differential equation:
x dy/dx = y − x tan(y/x)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: dy/dx = y/x − tan(y/x). Let y = vx ⇒ dy/dx = v + x dv/dx ⇒ v + x dv/dx = v − tanv ⇒ dv/tan v = −dx/x. Integrating both sides ⇒ ∫ cot v dv = −∫ dx/x ⇒ log|sin v| = −logx + logc ⇒ log|sin y/x| = −logx + logc = log c/x ⇒ x sin y/x = c

questions.text:
Solve the following differential equation:
(1 + x²) dy/dx + 2xy = 4x²
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: dy/dx + 2xy/(1+x²) = 4x²/(1+x²). Comparing with dy/dx + Py = Q: P = 2x/(1+x²), Q = 4x²/(1+x²). I.F. = e^∫(2x/(1+x²))dx = e^log(1+x²) = (1 + x²). Thus, the solution of the differential equation is, y(1 + x²) = ∫ 4x²/(1+x²) (1 + x²)dx ⟹ y(1 + x²) = 4x³/3 + c

questions.text:
A school offers students the choice of three modes for attending classes:
• Mode A: Offline (in-person) – 40% of students
• Mode B: Online (live virtual classes) – 35% of students
• Mode C: Recorded lectures – 25% of students
After a feedback survey:
• 20% of students from Mode A reported the class as “Excellent”
• 30% from Mode B rated it as “Excellent”
• 50% from Mode C rated it as “Excellent”
A student is selected at random from the entire group, and it is found that they rated the class as “Excellent.”
(a) Represent the data in terms of probability. Define the events clearly.
(b) Using Bayes’ Theorem, find the probability that the student attended the Recorded lectures (Mode C), given that they rated the class as “Excellent.”
(c) Interpret your result. Which mode has the highest likelihood of being chosen if a student says “Excellent”?
extractionIssues: The stem line 'A school offers students the choice of three modes for attending classes:' and 'After a feedback survey:' are missing from pdftotext output but present in the text layer (pdfplumber) and on the rendered page
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Let: A: student chose Mode A → P(A) = 0.40; B: student chose Mode B → P(B) = 0.35; C: student chose Mode C → P(C) = 0.25. Let E: student rated the class as Excellent. Given: P(E/A) = 0.20, P(E/B) = 0.30, P(E/C) = 0.50
(b) P(C/E) = P(C) × P(E/C) / [P(A) × P(E/A) + P(B) × P(E/B) + P(C) × P(E/C)] = 0.25 × 0.50 / [(0.40×0.20) + (0.35×0.30) + (0.25×0.50)] = 0.25 × 0.50 / [(0.08) + (0.105) + (0.125)] = 0.403
(c) There’s about a 40.3% chance that a student who rated the class as “Excellent” attended Recorded lectures. … By checking the numerators of P(C/E), P(B/E) and P(A/E) we observed 0.125 > 0.105 > 0.08. Therefore, recorded lectures (Mode C) have the highest likelihood of being the chosen mode among students who gave an excellent rating.

questions.text:
To raise money for an orphanage, students of three schools A, B and C organised an exhibition in their residential colony, where they sold paper bags, scrap books and pastel sheets made by using recycled paper. Student of school A sold 30 paper bags, 20 scrap books and 10 pastel sheets and raised ₹ 410. Student of school B sold 20 paper bags, 10 scrap books and 20 pastel sheets and raised ₹ 290. Student of school C sold 20 paper bags, 20 scrap books and 20 pastel sheets and raised ₹ 440.
Answer the following question:
(i) Translate the problem into a system of equations.
(ii) Solve the system of equation by using matrix method.
(iii) Hence, find the cost of one paper bag, one scrap book and one pastel sheet.
extractionIssues: Official answer matrices rebuilt inline row by row (rows separated by ';') from the rendered answer-key page; check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Let the cost of one paper bag, one scrap book and one pastel sheet be x, y and z respectively. 30x + 20y + 10z = 410 ⇒ 3x + 2y + z = 41; 20x + 10y + 20z = 290 ⇒ 2x + y + 2z = 29; 20x + 20y + 20z = 440 ⇒ x + y + z = 22
(ii) Given system of equations is equivalent to AX = B where A = [3 2 1; 2 1 2; 1 1 1], X = [x; y; z], B = [41; 29; 22]. |A| = −2 ≠ 0 ⇒ A⁻¹ exists. adj A = [−1 −1 3; 0 2 −4; 1 −1 −1]. Thus A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) adj A = −(1/2)[−1 −1 3; 0 2 −4; 1 −1 −1]. AX = B ⇒ X = A⁻¹B = [2; 15; 5] ∴ x = 2, y = 15, z = 5
(iii) The cost of one paper bag, one scrap book and one pastel sheet be Rs 2, Rs 15 and Rs 5 respectively.

questions.text: Evaluate: ∫ (x² + x + 1)/((x + 2)(x² + 1)) dx
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF (the text layer scrambles the stacked integrand)
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: Let: (x² + x + 1)/((x + 2)(x² + 1)) = A/(x + 2) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 1). Equating the coefficients of x², x and constant respectively, we get A + B = 1, 2B + C = 1, A + 2C = 1. Solving for A, B, C we get, C = 1/5, B = 2/5 and A = 3/5. ∴ ∫ (x² + x + 1)/((x + 2)(x² + 1)) dx = ∫ [3/(5(x + 2)) + (2x + 1)/(5(x² + 1))] dx. Integrating, we get = (3/5) ln|x + 2| + (1/5)[ln|x² + 1| + tan⁻¹(x)] + C

questions.text: Evaluate: ∫_{π/4}^{3π/4} x dx/(1+ sin x) dx
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF (limits π/4 to 3π/4 and stacked fraction; 'dx' appears both in the numerator and after the fraction, as printed)
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: I = ∫_{π/4}^{3π/4} x/(1 + sin x) dx. Here, a = π/4 and b = 3π/4, so a + b = π. Using ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x)dx: I = ∫_{π/4}^{3π/4} (π − x)/(1 + sin (π − x)) dx = ∫_{π/4}^{3π/4} (π − x)/(1 + sin x) dx. Adding, both integrals, I + I = ∫ (x + (π − x))/(1 + sin x) dx = π ∫ 1/(1 + sin x) dx ⟹ 2I = π ∫ (1−sin x)/(1− sin² x) dx = π ∫ (sec²x − secx tanx) dx ⟹ 2I = π[tanx − secx]_{π/4}^{3π/4}. I = (√2 − 1)π

questions.text:
A person has manufactured a water tank in the shape of a closed right circular cylinder. The volume of the cylinder is 539/2 cubic units. If the height and radius of the cylinder be h and r.
(a) Express h in terms of radius r and given volume.
(b) Let the total surface area of the closed cylinder tank be S, express S in term of radius r.
(c) If the total surface area of the tank is minimum, then prove that radius r = 7/2 units.
(d) Find the height of the tank.
extractionIssues: Figure on page 8 (cylinder labelled height(h), radius(r)) not reproduced; not needed to answer
Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text:
(a) volume V = πr²h; 539/(2πr²) = h
(b) S = 2πrh + 2πr²; S = 2πr · 539/(2πr²) + 2πr²; S = 2πr² + 539/r
(c) ds/dr = 4πr − 539/r². Setting ds/dr = 0 for stationary point, we get 539 = 4πr³; r = 7/2 unit. Now, d²s/dr² = 4π + (539×2)/r³ > 0, when r = 7/2 units. Therefore, the total surface area (S) of the tank is minimum when r = 7/2 units.
(d) h = 539/(2πr²) = (539×4×7)/(2×22×7×7) = 7 units.

questions.text:
A Dolphin jumps and taken a path given by the equation h(t) = (1/2)(−7t² + 3t + 2), (t ≥ 0), h(t) is the height of the Dolphin at any point of time.
(a) Is the function differentiable for t ≥ 0? Justify.
(b) Find the instantaneous rate of change of height at t = 1/14.
(c) h(t) is increasing in (−∞, 3/14). Is this true or false? Justify.
(d) Find the time at which the Dolphin will attains the maximum height. Also find the maximum height.
extractionIssues: Photograph on page 9 (image of a dolphin) not reproduced; not needed to answer
Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers/superscripts); check against the PDF
Official answer notation rebuilt from the rendered answer-key page (fractions/powers flattened in the text layer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text:
(a) h(t) = (1/2)(−7t² + 3t + 2), is a polynomial function, and all polynomial functions are continuous and differentiable everywhere on R. ∴ The function is differentiable for t ≥ 0.
(b) dh/dt = (1/2)(−14t + 3) = −7(t − 3/14). ∴ The instantaneous rate of change of height at t = 1/14 = [dh/dt] at t = 1/14 = 3/2 − 1/2 = 1 unit.
(c) dh/dt = −7(t − 3/14). Given, t ≥ 0. In (0, 3/14), dh/dt > 0. i.e., h(t) is increasing in (0, 3/14). ∴ h(t) is increasing in (−∞, 3/14). is false.
(d) Setting dh/dt = 0, for stationary point, we get −7(t − 3/14) = 0 ⇒ t = 3/14. Now, d²h/dt² = −7 < 0. ∴ h = f(t) has a local maximum at t = 3/14. ∴ Maximum height = [h(t)] at 3/14 = 1.161 units.

questions.text:

• The English teacher gives a test 90% of the time
• The Math teacher gives a test 80% of the time
• The Science teacher gives a test 70% of the time
Each teacher decides independently. If the average number of surprise tests is less than 2.3 then the teachers should coordinate better to increase the performance of the students. Otherwise, no action is needed.
Let X be the number of surprise tests a student gets on a given day.
So, X ∈ {0,1,2,3}.
(i) Find the probability for each possible number of surprise tests.
(ii) Use the probabilities to build a distribution table.
(iii) Calculate the average number of surprise tests per day.
(iv) Based on your calculations, decide: Should the teachers coordinate better? Or is the current plan acceptable?

questions.text:
A building is to be constructed in the form of a triangular pyramid ABCD as shown in the figure. Let the angular points be A (0, 1, 2), B (3, 0, 1), C (4, 3, 6) and D (2, 3, 2) and let G be the point of intersection of the medians of ∆BCD.

(a) What will be the length of vector AG⃗ ?
(b) Find the area of ∆ABC.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) G is the centroid of ∆BCD. The coordinates are ((3 + 4 + 2)/3, (0 + 3 + 3)/3, (1 + 6 + 2)/3) = (3,2,3). AG⃗ = (3 − 0)î + (2 − 1)ĵ + (3 − 2)k̂ = 3î + ĵ + k̂; |AG⃗| = √(3² + 1² + 1²) = √11 units
(b) AB⃗ = 3î − ĵ − k̂; AC⃗ = 4î + 2ĵ + 4k̂. Area of ∆ABC = (1/2)|AB⃗ × AC⃗|. AB⃗ × AC⃗ = |î ĵ k̂; 3 −1 −1; 4 2 4| = −2î − 16ĵ + 10k̂ and |AB⃗ × AC⃗| = 6√10. Hence area of ∆ABC = (1/2)|AB⃗ × AC⃗| = 3√10 sq units

officialAnswer.text: Method-I: Let the equation of the plane be a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) + c(z − z₁) = 0 is passing through (−1, 0, 2) ⇒ a(x + 1) + b(y – 0) + c(z – 2) = 0 …(1). Given line (x−0)/(−2) = (y−1)/3 = (z−1)/(−1) passing through (0, 1, 1) and having d.r. ⟨−2, 3, −1⟩. Since the plane contains the line and the point ⇒ a(1) + b(1) + c(1 – 2) = 0 ⇒ a + b – c = 0 …(2). Also the line and normal to the plane are perpendicular ⇒ –2a + 3b – c = 0 …(3). Solving (2) and (3) a/2 = b/3 = c/5 = k. Hence required equation of the plane is ⇒ 2(x + 1) + 3(y − 0) + 5(z − 2) = 0 ⇒ 2x + 3y + 5z − 8 = 0. Method–II: … required equation of the plane is |x+1 y z−2; 1 1 −1; −2 3 −1| = 0 ⇒ 2(x + 1) + 3(y − 0) + 5(z − 2) = 0 ⇒ 2x + 3y + 5z − 8 = 0

questions.text:
A real estate company is going to build a new residential complex. The land they have purchased can hold at the most 500 apartments. Also, if they make x apartments, then the monthly maintenance cost for the whole complex would be as follows:
Fixed cost = ₹ 4000
Variable cost = ₹ (14x − 0 ∙ 04x²)
How many apartments should the complex have in order to minimize the maintenance costs?

officialAnswer.text: C(x) = 4000 + 14x − 0.04x² ⇒ C′(x) = 14 − 0.08x. Now, C′(x) = 0 ⇒ 14 = 0.08x ⇒ x = 175. C″(x) = −0.08 < 0 ∴ C(x) will be maximum at x = 175. As per question, we have to minimise the maintenance cost. Since x can be 0 to 500 apartments, C(0) = 4000 + 14 × 0 − 0.04 × (0)² = 4000; C(500) = 4000 + 14 × 500 − 0.04 × (500)² = 1000 ∴ The complex must have 500 apartments to minimise the maintenance cost.
